instructions: Dice the onion, the carrots and 2 stalks of celery. Slice the mushrooms and mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium high. Add the onion, carrots and celery with 1/2 tsp salt and cook 5 to 7 minutes, stirring now and then, until they begin to soften.
Add the mushrooms and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until they have given off their liquid and turned golden brown.

Stir in the garlic and Italian seasoning and cook 30 seconds. Add the broth, 3 cups water, the barley and the soy sauce. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 25 to 30 minutes, until the barley is tender but still a little chewy.
Off the heat, stir in the vinegar, the pepper and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Chop 2 tbsp of the parsley and stir it in. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.

Serve hot. The barley keeps drinking the broth, so the soup thickens as it sits. Keep it in the fridge up to 5 days or in the freezer up to 3 months, and add a splash of broth or water when you reheat it until it's steaming.
method_notes: About 55 minutes, hands on for about 25 of them, and it reheats well, so it suits a weekend batch. Nothing found had 20 or more ratings, so this is a fallback lead: Salt & Lavender (5.0 from 8) sautés onion, carrot and celery, then mushrooms, and simmers with broth, water and pearl barley. A little soy sauce (The Nosher) and a splash of red wine vinegar at the end (The Yummy Vegan) add depth and brightness. Connoisseurus Veg and Monkey and Me make creamy versions with cashews or coconut; those were left out.
